answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil swarms by making every participant stake a refundable bond locked to a chain-verified identity, then charging each new identity a sequence of small proof-of-work or paid attestations before it may transact. A lone fake account starts at a nadir of trust, so spawning a thousand of them costs a thousand bonds plus a thousand attestation fees, all at risk of slashing. Reputation moves across that bridge slowly, letting honest agents reach a marble of verified standing while clones stay expensive and inert.
